If dark ever gets a real elevation channel, this is one of the two places it lands.

focus.$note: BUG FIX, not a restyle. The light halo was rgba(3, 0, 192, 0.38) — a violet-blue left over from the systemIndigo accent two accents ago — so every focus ring in the product bloomed a colour that appears nowhere else in the file, against a #0069d9 core. Nothing caught it: the validator iterates named colour tokens and never parses an rgba() inside a shadow string. Both values are now the theme's own focus.ring at reduced alpha (light #0069d9, dark #64b5ff), which is what the $comment on focus always said this was.

$shadowUsageNote: REVERSED 2026-08-13. It used to read: 'Elevation is still opt-in AT REST: a dashboard of tiles reads calmer flat, and every tile carrying a resting shadow was the look this system was built to avoid.' Every tile now carries shadow.card at rest, in light, by instruction — that resting float is the whole look. What survives the reversal is the LADDER, and it is the thing to protect. SPLIT 2026-08-14 into TWO ladders, because they used to share a rung and so neither could move: CARDS rest on shadow.card and raise to shadow.cardRaise; POPOVERS sit at shadow.lg and modals at shadow.xl. Previously hover and popover were both shadow.lg, which meant a deeper resting card was inexpressible — every value that restored the hover gap also restyled every menu in the product. .jrk-card--interactive:hover can only read as a raise if the resting shadow is visibly smaller than it, so the card ladder's two rungs must never be re-pointed at the same token and neither may be grown alone; the gap to hold is 3.3x by ambient weight (y-offset x alpha). If the ask is ever 'make the cards pop more' again, move BOTH card rungs and leave shadow.lg where it is — that is what the split is for. The old note's other half still holds and is why the hover rule keeps a fill as well: a shadow is invisible in dark, so surface.cardHover carries that theme alone.

size.$comment: macOS-compact, non-touch. These displays are 1920x1080 with a mouse, so the 44px touch target is dead weight — and 1080px of HEIGHT is the real constraint, which is why the vertical rhythm tightened too.

control.$note: md 28 -> 32 and lg 32 -> 40 on 2026-08-13. The airy look is mostly control height and horizontal padding, and a 28px pill reads as a chip rather than as a button. sm is UNMOVED at 24px because that is the WCAG 2.2 AA floor (2.5.8) and the $minTouchNote below is not a style position. The vertical cost is real and is the thing to watch — the $comment above is still true, 1080px of height is the binding constraint, and this spends 4px on every stacked control. Two callers were pinned rather than allowed to follow: .jrk-nav-item was on control-lg at 32px and is now explicitly on control-md to hold that height (the rail's own comment records 40px as already tried and rejected as touch-ergonomic), and the sheet's rows take size.sheet.*, which is a separate ladder and did not move at all. A dense report is still dense; it is the chrome around it that grew.

topbar.$note: 44px -> 56px, 2026-08-13. The tall white bar with room around its contents is the single most recognisable element of the reference look, and at 44px a 40px control (control-lg) has 2px of air above and below it. Paid for out of chrome, once, at the top of the page — not out of the content grid.

size.$removedCardEdgeNote: cardEdge (2px) is GONE with color.border.card — a tile is bounded by its fill step now, so there is no tile-edge weight to keep in one place. The five components that drew it (card, stat, stat band, chart card, sheet) each keep a 1px TRANSPARENT border instead of dropping the border shorthand entirely, so that a nested tile gaining its neutral hairline changes only a color and never reflows the layout by a pixel. Internal rules were always a hardcoded 1px and still are.
size.$minTouchNote: 24px is the WCAG 2.2 AA floor (2.5.8 Target Size Minimum), down from the 44px AAA touch target. Do not go below 24.

sheet.$comment: Spreadsheet density, tightened further for non-touch. Fixed track widths, because the Excel-style column bar can only line up with the data if every row shares one track list.
sheet.label: 98px

motion.$comment: Apple easing is a gentle ease-out; transitions are quick and small. All wrapped in the prefers-reduced-motion guard in base.css.
